purpose: Dimensionless visual calibration of KinoCFDDEM geometry from public imagery and official draw-video traceability.

observations.visual_description: Front/near-front view of two transparent spherical Kino draw machines. Article explicitly credits the image as a capture from Loteria de Concepcion / YouTube.
observations.measurement_method: manual visual pixel-ratio estimate from web-rendered source; conservative uncertainty includes perspective, acrylic rim and ball-edge ambiguity

observations.visual_description: Studio view showing two transparent spherical draw machines branded Kino/Chao Jefe.
observations.measurement_method: manual visual pixel-ratio estimate from web-rendered source; conservative uncertainty includes perspective and partial occlusion
traceability only in this iteration; direct frame bytes were not available to the numerical runtime

observations.fact: Kino draws 14 balls without replacement from 25 balls.
Loteria reported adding pre-draw ball weighing, ball measurement and tombola loading to draw recordings.

notes: The two quantitative observations are not independent metrology-grade measurements; their agreement is used only to constrain a dimensionless ratio.
Do not infer real ball diameter from unrelated lottery standards.
Do not fit mass, diameter or friction to winning numbers.
A real dimensional anchor visible in the same camera plane is required before changing the absolute CFD-DEM scale.
